answer: Each agent key is registered only after remote attestation binds it to an enclave running approved code, identified by MRENCLAVE, with platform evidence verified by the network. Assuming the key remains enclave-protected, duplicating a VM alone cannot create another trusted identity; an attacker must acquire genuine attestation-capable silicon and provision it. This raises the cost of Sybil identities: a voyage through a virtual inlet cannot replace timber anchored in physical hardware.
